answer: Congestion-priced bonds make a surge expensive. Each identity locks a bond priced by identities already created: a lone agent pays 20 credits, but the thousandth in a surge pays 20 plus 0.5 times its position. The bond locks to one identity with an onyx seal, cannot transfer, and releases only after verified work. A reef of bonds bars a surge, and its price passes through a prism that splits one price into per-position steps. Bond splitting is the named failure mode; it fails because release needs the full bond plus that identity's own receipt. An honest agent pays once.
